curriculum.lesson_evidence: Food safety stops germs from making people sick. Wash hands with soap and running water for at least 20 seconds before touching food, after using the toilet and after touching raw meat. Keep raw meat away from ready-to-eat food, keep cold food cold, cook food until it is hot all the way through and read use-by dates. Wash fruit and vegetables and use clean boards and utensils. Never share food with someone who has an allergy.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Rina uses the same knife to cut raw chicken and then tomatoes. What is the problem and what should she do instead?

FEEDBACK
Raw chicken can carry germs that spread to the tomatoes, which are eaten raw. She should use a separate knife and board, or wash them in hot soapy water between jobs, and wash her hands.

WATCH FOR
Thinking food is safe if it smells fine. Germs that cause illness often cannot be smelled or seen, so use safe steps and read dates.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Create a food safety poster for your kitchen with five rules, the hand washing steps and one use-by reminder. Time a 20-second hand wash (sing a song) and record how long it took. Use the poster with an adult at home.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teaching.feedback: The new situation should use the same PDHPE idea as the example, but happen in a different place or with different people.
teaching.fix: Change the choice or strategy, not just the wording.
teaching.guided_attempt: Describe or practise one fresh situation that uses the same skill and write a short reason for your choice.
teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new situation.
teaching.model: Food safety stops germs from making people sick. Wash hands with soap and running water for at least 20 seconds before touching food, after using the toilet and after touching raw meat. Keep raw meat away from ready-to-eat food, keep cold food cold, cook food until it is hot all the way through and read use-by dates. Wash fruit and vegetables and use clean boards and utensils. Never share food with someone who has an allergy. Now choose a different situation to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same PDHPE idea in a new place, game or situation, not a copy of the example. Review safety, fairness and inclusion.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
